palette.notes: grand northern capital: pale calcite and diorite walls with smooth-stone quoins and mullions on chiselled stone-brick plinths, deepslate-tile roofs, oxidised copper domes, spires and gutters, spruce and dark oak doors, shutters and stalls, deep blue banners; finer and taller toward the palace, plainer toward the walls

plots.brief: The smiths' green, ~20x14, the heart of the quarter just south of the mill pond: trampled grass and packed dirt with a quenching trough of stone, a great anvil on a stone plinth as a monument, benches of spruce slabs, two lime trees and a gravel apron on the lane side. Where apprentices race and the guild holds its summer fair. Detail: a well-worn bronze plaque in the anvil plinth listing masters' names, hung with lanterns on posts.

Coppersmith ~9x8, two storeys on the hill, stone ground floor with spruce upper, dark roof. Beaten pots and kettles hang across the shopfront; yard behind with a small crucible furnace. Detail: oxidised copper cap on the chimney and a hanging kettle sign.

Potter's house ~9x8, two storeys, terracotta-brown plaster over a stone plinth, dark oak frame. A domed brick kiln in the yard behind and shelves of pots in the open front. Detail: a row of drying jars along the windowsill.
Cutler's workshop ~9x8, two storeys, plain stone and dark oak, blackstone roof. Grindstone wheel under a lean-to outside, living quarters above. Detail: a giant iron-bar shears sign over the door.

Locksmith ~9x8, two storeys, narrow-windowed stone with iron-banded dark oak shutters, deepslate roof. Keys and padlocks in the shop window, bench with vice. Detail: a huge iron key hung as the shop sign.

Ironmonger ~10x8, two storeys, soot-streaked stone brick, spruce upper floor, blackstone roof. Barrels of nails and hinges stacked outside, small forge in the back. Detail: bundled iron rods leaning by the door and a smoking chimney.

Glazier's house ~9x9, two storeys, pale stone with spruce trim, slate roof, near the mill pond's west bank. Glass panes racked in a covered side bay, lead-casting hearth. Detail: coloured glass panes in the upper windows and a stained pane over the door.

Wood-turner ~9x8, two storeys, spruce and stone, dark oak roof. Pole lathe under an open lean-to, wood shavings and bowls in the window. Detail: carved wooden bobbin sign and a stack of seasoning timber.

Rope-maker ~9x8 house, two storeys, stone ground floor and spruce upper, dark roof, with a long open ropewalk shed along its west side. Coils of rope hang under the eaves. Detail: a spinning wheel on a post at the end of the walk.

Bell founder ~10x9, two storeys, stone brick with blackstone trim, a tall casting-house chimney, deepslate roof. Moulds and finished bells stand in the yard. Detail: a bell of copper hung in an open frame above the door.

Fletcher ~9x8, two storeys, spruce and plain stone, dark roof. Bows and arrow bundles on racks in the shop window, drying staves in a side yard. Detail: target butts at the back and a crossed-arrows sign.

Farrier's forge and stable ~10x8, two storeys, stone and dark oak, blackstone roof, with a hay-loft stable and paddock to the south. Open forge bay faces the lane. Detail: horseshoes nailed in a ring on the gable and a quench trough.

Iron store and weigh house ~11x9, two storeys, stone brick, spruce loading hoist, deepslate roof; a walled yard of ingot stacks. Ground floor store with a big cart door, clerk's rooms above. Detail: a giant balance scale as a sign over the doorway.

Guild hall of the smiths at the NW corner, ~11x9 walls, two storeys, stone-brick plinth with pale stone above and dark deepslate roof. Hammer-and-anvil banner in deep blue over a spruce double door; a small forecourt with an iron-bar railing. Detail: a weathered copper bell turret on the gable.

Forge, ~11x9, two storeys: open-fronted workshop below with a big stone chimney at the back, home above. Plain stone bricks, dark oak frame, blackstone roof. Detail: glowing furnace and anvil visible from the street, soot-dark chimney top with campfire smoke.

Carpenter's house ~11x8, two storeys, spruce and dark oak timber frame on a low stone plinth, deepslate roof. Walled yard behind with stacked logs, saw trestles and a drying shed. Detail: a hoist beam with a hanging crate over the upper door.

Mason's lodge ~10x8, two storeys, pale stone and chiselled stone trim; a yard with stone blocks, a crane (spruce fence arm) and a half-carved column. Dark slate roof. Detail: statue in progress on a plinth by the door.

Foundry, ~12x9, wide two-storey hall in plain stone brick with two tall chimneys, blackstone roof, big arched double doors. Detail: casting pit visible through a grille and a stack of ingots; soot-stained walls (cobblestone and blackstone mix).

Glassworks at the NE corner near the river, ~11x9, two storeys, pale stone with a domed kiln chimney. Tall windows with stone mullions, glass panes displayed in the shopfront. Detail: stained-glass transom over the door and a copper-capped chimney.

Cooper's house ~9x10, two storeys on the low hill's flank, spruce and stone, dark roof. Barrels stacked in the side yard, hoops on a drying rack. Detail: a giant barrel used as a shop sign above the door.

Weaver's house ~10x10, two storeys on the hill, wool-white and gray plaster over stone plinth, dark roof. Loom room with big windows on ground floor, wool bales out front. Detail: blue and white striped cloth hung from an upper balcony.

Dyer's house ~10x10, two storeys, stone ground floor with spruce upper floor. Side yard of coloured dye vats (cauldrons) and a drying rack of hung wool in many colours. Detail: bright stains on the plinth and a deep blue banner.
Tanner's house ~10x10, two storeys, plain stone and spruce, dark roof. Hide-stretching frames and a tanning pit in the yard at the east side. Detail: hides draped over a rack and a leather sign.
Wheelwright ~11x8, two storeys, spruce frame on stone plinth, dark roof. Cart wheels leaning in a yard and a half-built wagon. Detail: a big wheel mounted on the gable.

Chandler's house ~10x8, two storeys, pale stone with spruce shutters, dark roof. Candles in every window, rendering vats in a back yard. Detail: lantern-lit shopfront and bundled candles hung under the porch.

Open timber yard with a long stone-plinth office-house ~10x8, two storeys, spruce and dark oak. Stacked planks, a sawpit and a log pile on the north side. Detail: water-driven log pulley hints toward the pond.

plots.type: dye works near the mill pond
plots.brief: Dye works ~12x9, two storeys, stone with spruce upper floor and wide shuttered drying loft under the roof. Rows of drying racks with coloured cloth between this plot and the pond, vats by the door. Detail: coloured streaks on the plinth and a pulley for hoisting cloth.

Fulling mill ~12x9 on the river side, two storeys, stone ground floor and dark oak upper, with a water wheel on the east flank dipping toward the river. Stamping beams inside. Detail: the wheel and a sluice channel, wool hanging to dry on the roof lines.

Timber wharf on the river bank: a warehouse ~12x8 of spruce on a stone plinth, with a wooden jetty extending east into the river (raft logs tied alongside) and a crane arm. Detail: stacked rafts and a rope-and-lantern post at the jetty end.

Customs house, about 13x11 walls, two storeys on a stone-brick plinth at y 65, fronting Harbour Street (door north under a small calcite portico). Diorite and calcite walls, deepslate roof, tall mullioned windows, a blue banner and a scales-and-seal sign; a barred spruce loading hatch on the south face toward the warehouses.

Fish market hall, about 15x10, open-sided: stone-brick piers and a long dark-slate roof on spruce posts, stone slab counters with barrels and cauldrons of water, a gutter channel down the middle of the floor. Open to Harbour Street on the north; hanging lanterns and a fish-shaped weathervane on the ridge.

Sailors' chapel on the spur's north rise at y 74, about 9x11 walls with a nave and a small apse toward the lake (south). Calcite and stone brick on a chiselled plinth, steep deepslate roof, a slender oxidised-copper spirelet with a ship weathervane, stained-glass blue windows; door north under a small gabled porch with a hanging ship's bell. Steps climb up from Harbour Street.

Harbourmaster's house on the eastern shoulder of the spur at y 71, about 9x9 walls, two storeys, stone-brick base and diorite walls, dark roof, door north to Harbour Street under a spruce porch; chart-room bay window looking to the lake, a signal mast with flags on the roof and a stone retaining wall on the downhill side.

The ropewalk: a long low shed about 20x6 walls, one storey, open slatted spruce sides, stone-brick end piers, a long dark roof with a lantern vent; rope-twisting frames and coils inside, door north on Harbour Street, a drying yard of posts along the south wall.

Sailors' lodgings, about 14x11 walls, two storeys with a row of small dormers, whitewashed diorite on a stone plinth at y 63, spruce door north on Harbour Street with a lantern and a ship's-lantern sign; shuttered windows, a chimney stack, dormitory beds upstairs.

Ship chandler's shop, about 7x7 walls, two storeys, shop front with a wide shuttered window and a hanging anchor sign, door east onto the harbour avenue; coils of rope, barrels and lanterns on display under a plank awning. Whitewashed diorite on a stone plinth, dark roof.

The Harbour: a walled stone quay about 35x16 whose east end meets the harbour avenue at y 63, its south half over the lake. Stone-brick quay wall on a cut-stone plinth, two spruce piers running south into the water with bollards and lanterns, a lake gate (arched, with portcullis and blue banners) at the south end, a hoist crane of spruce on the east quay, stone steps down to the waterline. Working and plain, not ornate; a copper-capped harbour-master's booth at the landward east corner by the avenue.

Net-mending green, about 21x19, the quarter's open heart: trodden grass and gravel with spruce drying racks hung with nets, a stone-brick well, benches, barrel stacks and a few upturned boats on trestles. Edged by low stone kerbs, lanterns on spruce posts at the corners; entered from lane 1 on the west. Left unroofed.

Quayside warehouse, about 11x7 walls plus loading apron, one tall storey, stone-brick plinth, calcite and diorite walls, dark slate roof, a spruce hoist beam jutting from the gable with a rope and hook, big spruce double doors east onto lane 1.

Bonded warehouse, about 11x7 walls, one storey with a loft, stone-brick plinth, diorite walls, dark roof, hoist beam with pulley over a high loft door, barrels and crates stacked by the spruce double doors on lane 1.

Shipwrights' guildhall on the spur's lower shoulder, about 9x6 walls, one storey plus loft, stone-brick plinth stepped into the slope, diorite walls, dark roof, door north to lane 2 under a spruce porch; a ship's-model sign and a slipway of spruce rails outside.

Signal house and pilots' watch, about 5x9 walls on the spur's west flank, two storeys, stone-brick base with diorite upper floor, dark roof, a lookout bay on the lake side with a lantern on a spruce post; door east on lane 3.

Harbour lighthouse on the spur's southern rock, base about 9x9 walls, a tapering tower of white and stone-brick bands about 22 blocks tall, a lantern room with glass and glowstone under a dark conical cap; a keeper's lean-to and spruce door on the west by lane 3, rocky foreshore below.

The Anchor, sailors' tavern about 17x8 walls, two storeys on a stone plinth, diorite walls with spruce framing and a dark roof, wide spruce door on the west under a swinging anchor sign, taproom with barrel tables, a chimney, a long bench-lined yard on the south side.

Net and sail loft, about 15x5 walls, a long low shed on stone footings by the shore, calcite and spruce slats, dark roof with a hatch and hoist beam on the gable, rolls of canvas and nets hung inside; door west on lane 1.

Four-storey stone town house (about 7x8 walls) on a chiselled-stone-brick plinth, fronting the King's Way with a colonnaded ground floor of smooth-stone columns and a spruce door under the arcade. Calcite walls, tall mullioned windows, deepslate-tile roof with copper gutters and a small copper-capped corner turret. Its east flank looks across the sinkhole garden: give that side a balcony with a deep blue banner.

Four-storey diorite and stone-brick town house (about 7x8 walls), twin of its northern neighbour but mirrored: colonnaded ground floor on the King's Way, dark oak shutters, deepslate-tile roof, oxidised copper spire on the street corner. Chimney on the east wall; a garden-side oriel window over the sunken garden.

Three-storey town house (about 10x8 walls) at the garden's south-east corner, door on the plateau road behind a pillared porch, with a tall north-facing windowed hall and balcony overlooking the sinkhole garden and fountain. Calcite and smooth stone on a plinth, deepslate-tile roof, copper dome on a small garden-side bay.

Three-storey stone house (about 10x8 walls) fronting the plateau road with a stepped stone stoop and arched spruce door; chiselled-stone string courses between floors, mullioned windows, steep deepslate roof with two dormers and copper gutters. Small walled yard behind (north) with a pear tree.

Four-storey stone house (about 10x8 walls), the tallest of the plateau-road row, with a stone-bricks plinth, arched ground-floor loggia on the road, a blue banner on each side of the door, a deepslate roof and a slim oxidised copper spire at the east corner.

Three-storey stone house (about 9x8 walls) facing Harbour Avenue on the east, with a colonnaded ground-floor arcade, calcite walls, dark oak shutters and a deepslate-tile roof with a copper-clad lantern. Its west side overlooks the quiet upper garden lawn.

Westernmost town house, about 11x10 walls on an 18x22 plot, four storeys of pale stone on a chiselled plinth, door north onto the south ring under a carved stone door case. Symmetrical facade with tall mullioned windows, copper gutters and a deepslate roof. The south side steps down through a small walled back garden to a terrace looking over the river where it leaves the city; one detail: an oxidised copper oriel at the river corner.

Town house about 11x10 walls on an 18x22 plot, three to four storeys, door north onto the south ring, stone door case with spruce door and blue banner. Ordered symmetrical facade with stone mullions, copper gutters, deepslate tile roof with twin chimneys. Walled back garden to the south with a fruit tree and a gate; one detail: a copper-roofed bay over the door.

Fine town house about 11x10 walls on a 23x13 plot, four storeys, door east onto the King's Way with a carved stone door case and steps up from the avenue. Calcite and diorite facade with smooth-stone quoins, tall mullioned windows, copper gutters, dark deepslate roof; small walled garden behind to the west toward the river. One detail: a copper-capped corner turret facing the south ring.

Fine town house about 11x10 walls on a 23x12 plot, three to four storeys, door east onto the King's Way matching its northern neighbour in symmetry but with a bow window above the door. Pale stone on a cut-stone plinth, copper gutters, deepslate roof, walled back garden to the west. One detail: a blue banner pair and wall lanterns flanking the door case.

The Grand Market: a paved square about 30x30 on level ground at y 69, opening north onto the west avenue (its entrance gate is the north side, an arch of calcite pillars with blue banners). Pale stone paving in a chequer of smooth stone and stone bricks, a central three-tier fountain with an oxidised copper finial, a market cross on steps near the Kings Way end, and two rows of spruce and dark-oak stalls with blue-and-white striped awnings leaving a clear processional lane from the avenue to the south. Lamp posts at the corners. Keep the south edge (toward z 197) open: Kings Way enters here.

Quay warehouse, about 11x9 walls, two storeys with a hoist beam, on a cut-stone plinth at the river quay. Plain stone-brick walls, dark deepslate roof, big spruce loading doors facing market-west street (door west) and a crane arm with a rope over the road; a small stone landing step by the water.

Tall merchant's house, three storeys, about 11x10 walls, shop front with arched windows on the ground floor (door west onto the quay street) and a hanging sign; calcite upper floors with stone mullion windows and blue banners, deepslate roof with a copper gutter. The east face fronts the square with shuttered windows and a first-floor balcony over the stalls.

The Quay Inn, about 12x11 walls, three storeys with a steep deepslate roof and dormers, pale stone on a chiselled plinth. Door west onto the quay street under a spruce porch with a lantern and a painted sign (a blue heron); stable arch on the south side, tap-room windows toward the river, a copper-clad chimney.

Longer quay warehouse, about 12x10 walls, two storeys, partly on piles over the river edge. Stone-brick and dark-oak frame, wide loading doors to the quay street (west) with a wooden jetty on piles and a hoist gable. Plainer than the market buildings: it is working space.

The Merchants' Guildhall, the district's second landmark: about 12x18 walls, two storeys over an arcaded ground floor, fine calcite and diorite on a chiselled-stone plinth. The long north face looks onto the square across a row of round-arched arcades (open loggia, columns of smooth stone); the formal door is south toward the south ring road, under a blue banner and a stone pediment. A copper-capped clock tower of ~5x5 base rises about 10 blocks above the roof at the north-east corner, oxidised copper spire and four clock faces. Deepslate-tile roof, copper gutters, tall mullioned windows in the hall.

The Corn Exchange: a broad hall about 14x17 walls, one tall storey with a long pale-stone arcaded front on the square side and clerestory windows, stone-brick on a plinth, a low deepslate roof with a copper lantern ridge. Main door south on the ring road under a wheatsheaf carving (hay-bale and wheat details), open trading floor inside with counters of spruce.

The Lion's Rest, a compact inn about 9x8 walls, three storeys, calcite with smooth-stone quoins and a steep deepslate roof. Door east onto market-east street under a spruce porch with a blue banner and a hanging lion sign; an upstairs window overlooks the square across the lane.

Tall merchant's house, three storeys, about 9x10 walls, with a shop front and awning on the ground floor (door east onto market-east street). Pale stone, dark-oak shutters, blue banners, a copper-capped corner turret, deepslate roof; the west face looks onto the square from a stone balcony.

Three-storey merchant's house, about 9x10 walls, a goldsmith's: arched shop window, wrought-iron sign bracket, door east onto market-east street. Diorite and calcite with chiselled-stone plinth, tall mullioned windows, stepped gable to the street and a deep-blue banner on each floor.

The merchants' bank on the corner where the market-east street meets West Avenue, about 16x16 with roof overhang room, three storeys. Calcite and diorite on a chiselled stone-brick plinth with smooth-stone quoins, deepslate-tile roof and a small oxidised-copper cupola on the corner. Ground-floor banking hall behind an arcade of three tall arches facing the market (door west), strongroom with iron bars above, blue banners either side of the door. Detail: a copper-gilded scale sign hanging over the door.

Tall three-storey merchant house, about 9x9 walls on a 14x14 plot, fronting West Avenue (door north). Ground-floor counting room with big mullioned windows, storeys above are warehouse lofts with a hoist beam and loading hatch under the gable. Calcite and diorite, smooth-stone trim, dark oak shutters, deepslate roof. Twin to merchants_house_n2 across the garden; detail: copper gutters and a hanging shop sign.

A small public garden on the south bank of the little pond just north (around x -2482), about 17x14, entered from West Avenue. Stone-brick paths, low calcite walls, hedges of azalea leaves, flowering beds, two benches of spruce stairs and a small copper-roofed pavilion by the water. Detail: a tiny stone footbridge or stepping stones at the pond edge.

Small two-storey money-changers' shop, about 8x6 walls on a 13x10 plot, on Copper Lane near the market-east street (door south). Pale stone with a barred counter window facing the lane, dark oak shutters, deepslate roof. Detail: a scales-and-coins sign in copper and a small strongbox alcove visible through the window.

Tall three-storey merchant house, about 9x9 walls on a 14x14 plot, fronting the market-east street (door west). Ground-floor shop with open arcade bay, counting room behind, warehouse lofts above with a hoist. Calcite and diorite on a stone plinth, smooth-stone trim, dark oak shutters, deepslate roof. Pair with merchants_house_w2; give this one a stepped gable. Detail: blue banner on a bracket.

Three-storey merchant house, about 9x8 walls on a 14x13 plot, second of the pair on the market-east street (door west). Counting room below, warehouse lofts above, calcite and diorite with smooth-stone trim and dark oak shutters, deepslate roof with a different gable than its twin to the north. Detail: a copper gutter and downspout and a crane arm over the loft door.

Wealthy three-storey merchant house, about 10x9 walls on a 15x14 plot, facing the east ring street (door east), with a small forecourt. Shop and counting room on the ground floor, warehouse lofts above, calcite with diorite banding, smooth-stone trim, dark oak shutters, deepslate roof. Detail: a copper-roofed oriel window on the first floor.

Three-storey merchant house, about 10x8 walls on a 15x13 plot, twin of merchants_house_e1 on the east ring street (door east). Counting room below, lofts above with a hoist beam, calcite and diorite, smooth-stone trim, dark oak shutters, deepslate roof. Detail: a blue banner and a lantern-lit door with a stone step.

Tall three-storey merchant house, about 10x9 walls on a 15x14 plot, on Copper Lane (door south). Open arcaded shop bay on the ground floor, counting room behind, warehouse lofts above. Calcite and diorite on a chiselled plinth, smooth-stone trim, dark oak shutters, deepslate roof. Detail: copper downspouts and a goods-crane over a loft door.

Smithy just inside the north gate: stone-brick ground floor open to an forge yard on the avenue side, calcite upper room, deepslate roof with a tall stone chimney. Detail: an anvil and quench trough under a lean-to by the door.

Two-and-a-half storey gatehouse inn on the avenue, ~12x9 walls: stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof, stable arch to a rear yard. Detail: dark oak hanging sign and a blue banner over the door.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, plain calcite upper floor, deepslate gable roof facing the ring road. Detail: one spruce shutter pair.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: window boxes with blue flowers.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick plinth, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a stone step and lantern by the dark oak door.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a small chimney with a copper cap.
Two-storey corner town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a blue banner on the corner.
Two-storey end house by the east ring road, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a small walled back yard toward the pond.

Bakery on the avenue, ~8x8 walls, two storeys: shop and oven below in stone brick, baker's rooms above in calcite, deepslate roof. Detail: a big stone chimney and a spruce counter shutter opening to the street.
Small paved well square ~11x11 of stone bricks and smooth stone: a stone well with a deepslate roof and copper cap in the middle, benches, two trees in planters, blue banners on lamp posts.

Plain parish church, ~15x11 walls, nave with a small apse, calcite on a stone-brick plinth, tall mullioned windows, deepslate roof and a square bell tower with an oxidised copper spire, doors on the square. Detail: a rose window of stained glass.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof, facing the church. Detail: a small gate in a low stone wall.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a vine on a spruce trellis.
Two-storey town house on the avenue, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a blue banner.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: spruce shutters.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: flower boxes.
Two-storey town house facing the west avenue, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a corner quoin of smooth stone.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: tall mullioned front window.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: dark oak door with lantern.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: copper gutter along the eave.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a small bread-oven chimney.

Village green ~16x12 fenced with low stone-brick walls and a gate on the spine lane: lawn, a gravel cross path, four oaks, a stone bench ring around a small pump, a notice board. Flat and plain; the heart of the quarter.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, plain calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a stone step and lantern by the door.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, plain calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: spruce shutters and a small chimney.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, plain calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: window boxes of blue flowers.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, plain calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a vine on a spruce trellis.
Two-storey town house facing the green, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a low walled front garden.
Two-storey town house on lane 1, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a blue banner by the door.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a copper-capped chimney.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a tall mullioned front window.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a small bread-oven chimney.
Two-storey town house, ~7x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a dark oak door with lantern.
Narrow two-storey town house facing lane 1, ~6x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: smooth stone quoins.
Narrow two-storey town house facing lane 2, ~6x7 walls, stone-brick ground floor, calcite upper, deepslate roof. Detail: a hanging flower basket.

Three-storey stone watermill, about 11x9 walls on a chiselled plinth, standing half over the river so its undershot wheel (spruce, 6 blocks across) turns on the west face in the current. Pale stone with spruce timber and a deepslate-tile roof, a small copper-roofed hoist gable over the loading door on the quay side (east). Sacks and a hoist beam on the quay; one blue banner.

Long boathouse about 14x8 walls, the west half on spruce piles over the river with an open slip and a raised arched water gate; stone ground floor to the quay, a store loft above under a low deepslate roof. Plain, little trim; rowing boats and a hanging lantern at the slip.

A net-loft boathouse about 14x8, half over the river, with one tall spruce-boarded loft and a hoist beam above the slip. Stone quay-side office with a shuttered window; nets drying on racks beside the door.

plots.type: water stairs and covered footbridge landing
plots.brief: The district's one special detail: a broad flight of stone water stairs (7 wide) stepping down into the river, flanked by a small covered landing about 8x6 with a spruce-beamed roof on stone piers and a deep blue banner, from which a covered spruce footbridge on piers starts out toward the west bank (the bridge itself is built later). Mooring rings and a bench under the roof.

Long stone barge warehouse about 13x11 walls, two storeys, plain pale stone on a stone-brick plinth with spruce timber doors and a loading hoist over the quay (west). Deepslate roof, few windows, tall cargo doors; barrels and crates stacked beside the quay.

Second warehouse about 13x11, two storeys, with a stepped stone gable end and three wide spruce loading doors onto the quay (west), an upper hoist door. Plain stone, deepslate roof; a clerk's lean-to office at the north corner.

Brewery about 13x11 walls, two storeys, with a tall stone chimney and a louvred malting-loft gable; stone ground floor with arched cart doors facing the quay (west), spruce timber loft above. Hop poles and barrels in the yard; the detail is a copper brewing-kettle roof lantern over the brewhouse.

The quay's finest plain building: about 12x9, two tall storeys of smooth stone and diorite with stone-mullioned windows, a small oxidised-copper gutter line and a spruce door under a shallow arcade of three arches facing the quay (west). Deepslate roof; scales and a deep blue banner beside the door.

Plain terraced house about 9x9 walls, two storeys on a low stone plinth, calcite walls with spruce shutters and door, deepslate roof running parallel to the avenue (door east). Window boxes, a stone chimney on the party wall; first of the terrace.

Terraced house about 9x9, three storeys and narrow, pale stone with spruce window frames, deepslate roof, door east with two steps. Slightly taller than its neighbours; a copper downpipe and a hanging sign.
Terraced house about 9x9, two storeys with an attic dormer, diorite and stone-brick walls, spruce door and shutters, deepslate roof. Chimney at the south party wall; a small herb bed beside the door.

Terraced house about 9x9, two storeys, plain pale stone with spruce timber and a deepslate roof; a ground-floor shopfront window (a chandler or rope-maker) with a spruce shutter that folds into a counter, door east.
End-of-terrace house about 10x9, two storeys, with a side garden wall and a gated archway through to the quay lane; pale stone, spruce door, deepslate roof, one blue banner on the corner.

Shallow, long tannery about 18x8 walls, one storey plus loft, plain stone with spruce drying racks and a louvred loft; the yard's soaking pits (stone-lined cauldron vats) face the river on the west side, hides hung on spruce frames. Low deepslate roof, door east to the avenue.

Open-sided market hall about 18x10 on stone piers: a long deepslate roof on stone posts over spruce stalls with stone slab counters, a gutter line in oxidised copper; the west end opens onto a stepped landing at the river. Banner at each end; the southern end of the quays, beside the west-avenue.

The district's quiet centre: a grassed quay green about 15x13 on the low west bank where the lanes meet, ringed by a low stone kerb. A spruce-roofed well in the middle, two benches, net-drying posts, three pollarded trees in stone planters and a mooring stone by the water; a plain stone path from the lane to the river. One blue banner on a post.

Plain two-storey house about 9x8 walls on a 15x11 plot, pale stone with spruce timber and a deepslate roof, door south onto the quay lane. A ropewalk lean-to on the west side, coils and floats in the window, a hanging rope sign. Little trim.

Small one-and-a-half-storey stone ferryman's house about 7x7 walls on an 11x10 plot, door west onto the lane. Spruce shutters, deepslate roof, a bell on a post and a lantern by the door; a stone path runs on to a spruce ferry pier on piles out over the water, with a moored ferry boat.

Low cooperage about 8x7 walls, stone ground floor with a spruce-timber loft, deepslate roof, door west onto the lane. Barrels and hoop racks in a fenced side yard; a hoist beam over the loft door. The waterward side stands on piles with a small dock for barrel boats.

plots.type: net shed boathouse over the water
plots.brief: Shallow boat and net shed about 8x5 walls, partly on spruce piles over the river bend at the south end of the lane; stone landward end, spruce-boarded seaward end, low deepslate roof, an open slip with rowing boats and nets on racks. Door west onto the lane.

The palace, about 44x36 walls on the highest ground, three to four storeys, calcite and smooth stone on a chiselled-brick plinth, four corner towers with deepslate cones, a central oxidised-copper dome, tall mullioned windows and a colonnaded ground floor. Gate on the north face, centred on the King's Way axis (x -2556), reached by broad stone steps and terraces (calcite balustrades, paired blue banner poles, a pair of copper-roofed gate lodges at the foot) rising about 10 blocks from the plateau road. Allow 2 blocks all round for roof overhangs and steps. Special detail: a great arched gate with blue banners and a copper-gutter cornice.

Cathedral about 36x22 with a nave running east-west, a deep north porch and portal facing the plateau road, a west front toward the close (the open ground between palace and cathedral), transepts, tall mullioned windows, deepslate-tile roof and a very tall oxidised-copper spire, the city's tallest structure. Allow 2 blocks all round for buttresses, porch and steps. Special detail: a rose window over the west front and a deep pointed north portal with spruce doors.

Bishop's palace fronting Harbour Avenue, 13x9 walls, three storeys, calcite with smooth stone quoins and a deepslate roof, stepped gables, a cloister walk on the south side with an arcade of stone columns. Special detail: a small copper-roofed oriel chapel on the corner facing the cathedral.

Narrow tall house for the royal scribes, 5x11 walls, three storeys, stone bricks and calcite with very tall windows and a deepslate roof, set between chancery and garden on Harbour Street. Special detail: a copper gutter line and a hanging lantern sign over the door.

Royal guard barracks around a small drill yard, 18x11 outer walls, two storeys, plain stone bricks and diorite, deepslate roof, dark oak doors, an arrow-slit tower on the cliff corner overlooking the harbour. Gate on the south face toward Harbour Street. Special detail: an armoury forge chimney and a blue banner over the gate.

Chancery of state, 16x10 walls, two to three storeys, calcite and smooth stone with tall mullioned windows over a chiselled-brick plinth, front colonnade of six columns facing Harbour Street. Special detail: a copper-capped clock turret above the entrance.

Upper terraces of the royal garden in the dip (ground 62-64): hedges of azalea and leaves, flower beds in blue and white, gravel paths, a pergola of spruce and a belvedere pavilion with a copper roof on the north edge. Entrance gate on the east side from Harbour Avenue. Retaining walls of stone brick. Special detail: a stair of stone down the middle to the basin.

Lower garden with a long fountain basin (about 20x4, quartz-edged, water with jets), lawns, clipped hedges and benches, and a wide stair down toward Harbour Street to the south. Special detail: a statue of the first king on a plinth at the basin end.

The Great Library: ~30x20 walls on this 34x22 plot, three storeys on a cut-stone plinth with a copper dome over the central stair hall and a long reading hall along the south side with tall mullioned windows. Pale stone, deepslate roof, an arcade along the front, deep blue banners, spruce doors. Faces the west avenue with broad steps up from the street.

Observatory crowning the hill: a round pale-stone tower ~9 wide and 5 storeys with an oxidised copper dome and an opening slit, on a terraced plinth with a low wall around a star-gazing terrace. A stair path climbs from the avenue door. Plainer than the library; a copper armillary sphere on the terrace is the special detail.

Masters' house of two storeys, ~10x8, on the shoulder of the hill beside the library: pale stone, steep deepslate roof, bay window, spruce door and shutters, a chimney and a small walled kitchen garden behind.

Printing house, 2 storeys ~12x9: wide ground-floor shopfront windows in spruce frames, a loft with a hoist beam over the door, paper drying racks under the eaves, stone bricks on a plinth, deepslate roof.
Hostel for visiting students, two storeys ~10x8, at the river end of the quarter: pale stone, dark oak shutters, small dormers, a lantern-hung porch with a bench.
School house ~14x10, one tall hall storey with a bell turret: plain pale stone, big mullioned windows, deepslate roof, a walled yard with a well. Door on the ring-road side.
Apothecary, two storeys ~11x8: stone-brick base, pale plaster upper floor, a hanging sign and jar-filled window boxes, a fenced herb plot at the side with a cauldron, copper gutters.
Masters' house ~12x9 with a south-facing walled garden toward the river; two storeys, pale stone and spruce, gabled roof, a study bay window capped in copper.

Garden square between library and college: paved in stone bricks and polished andesite in quarters around a central round fountain, clipped hedges, benches, lanterns on posts, trees at the corners. Pedestrian square reached from the library steps and the college; no street door.

The College around a cloistered courtyard: ~34x22 walls on this plot. Two-storey pale-stone ranges on all four sides with an arcaded cloister walk, a garden and well in the court, a gatehouse tower on the south street side with a copper cap, dark oak doors, deep blue banners. Plainer than the library.
Riverside masters' house ~9x8, two storeys, pale stone with a spruce porch and a terrace garden stepping down toward the river view.
Masters' house ~9x8, one and a half storeys, with a bay window and a copper-roofed oriel, hedge-walled garden behind facing the river.

Small open reading pavilion on the river bank at the quarter's south-east corner: stone colonnade, copper roof, steps down to the water and a bench terrace looking out where the river leaves the city.
Physic garden walled in stone bricks, ~15x18: herb beds in quartered pattern, a copper gate arch, a sundial and a gardener's shed. Entered from the garden square.
Bookbinder's workshop, one storey with a loft ~11x9, facing the garden square: stone and spruce, skylight in the roof, a stack of leather and paper under a lean-to.

gates.note: on the ridge top, beside the observatory hill
the river enters the city under an arch
the river leaves the city toward the lower river
the harbour's sea-gate onto the lake

wall.notes: follows the land: the west ridge (70-82) on the west, the north wall across gentle 63-72 ground, the east river bank on the east, the lake shore on the south, and the ravine cliff on the plateau's west side (the plateau needs only a parapet there). Around z 184-200 the east wall line stands in the river's edge: build it on the bank.
